//: Copy to config.json and fill in. config.json is gitignored, so never commit it.

event.//key: TBA event key. CalGames 2026 is expected to be 2026cacg. Confirm on thebluealliance.com before the event.
event.//name: Event name as it appears in titles, following the official FIRST channel convention: 'Qualification 1 - CalGames', 'Match 1 (R1) - CalGames', 'Final Tiebreaker - CalGames'. Livestreams read '2026 CalGames - Day 1'.
event.name: CalGames
event.//resultsUrl: Linked in every video description. Blank omits the line.

game.//: Bonus RP thresholds. Off-season events move these, and the 2026 REBUILT numbers were still being argued over while this was built. They travel on the state snapshot, so changing one here changes the reducer, every badge, and the talent view together. Defaults below match the REBUILT constants in apps/core/src/types.ts.

kiosk.//fieldStreamUrl: Field picture for pit monitors at /s/watch. A YouTube live URL, an MJPEG stream off a capture box, or any video URL a browser plays. Blank draws the CalGames backdrop instead. Served to the open pit-monitor pages through /api/urls, so never point it at anything you would not put on a projector.

publish.//enabled: Master switch. Nothing uploads while this is false.
publish.//mode: deferred | trickle | live. Keep deferred during competition: the live stream must never compete with an upload for the venue uplink. Measure the uplink on Friday before changing this.
publish.//autoQueuePractice: Practice matches queue automatically too ('Practice 3 - CalGames'). They upload but never link on TBA, which has no keys for practice. Set false to keep Friday load-in off the channel; queueing one by hand from the desk always works regardless.
publish.//autoQueueArcade: Each finished arcade set queues as its own segment video, titled like 'Arcade Winners Semifinal (Smash)', from the set's start to when it ended.
publish.//privacy: Videos upload unlisted and flip to public only once TBA linking succeeds, so a failed link never leaves an orphan video with no context.
publish.//playlists: YouTube playlist IDs (PL...). Leave blank to skip playlist insertion.
publish.//credit: Closing lines of every description, mirroring the official channel's layout. FIRST's own videos end '(c) 2026 FIRST Robotics Competition' (that is theirs to claim). CalGames is a WRRF off-season event, so these default to WRRF.
publish.credit: Uploaded by the CalGames Content Desk

recording.//: What the rolling recorder captures when the desk is launched with --record. One entry per feed: role 'program' is the composited broadcast (what uploads are cut from), role 'iso' is a raw camera (replay source only). 'input' is the ffmpeg input arguments as an array. A malformed entry is skipped with a warning at startup, never a crash. --test-sources ignores this list and records color bars instead.

audio.//: House audio: the room's PA, and only the room's PA. Nothing here can reach the stream. The two-bus rule in docs/06 is a cable, not a setting, and this is a control surface for the machine that already had the music on it.
audio.//enabled: Walk-up clips and stingers work with this on and nothing else configured: they play off this disk, with no internet and no account.
audio.//spotify: Optional background playlist. Requires a Spotify PREMIUM account (remote control does not work on free), and read the licensing note in docs/06 before using it at a public event.
audio.//clientId: From developer.spotify.com/dashboard. Not a secret: PKCE needs none.
audio.//refreshToken: Run: npm run auth:spotify. Expires six months after it is minted, used or not.
audio.//deviceName: The name the music machine's Spotify shows under Connect. Blank drives whatever device is already active.

sponsors.//: Who paid for this. Tier decides how often a sponsor comes round in the rotation (title 3x, major 2x, supporting 1x), never how big it is drawn.
sponsors.//report: GET /api/sponsors?report=1 gives pasteable text: appearances and seconds on screen per sponsor, counted from the broadcast itself.
sponsors.//logo: Optional path under /media, e.g. /media/sponsors/acme.png. The name is always drawn, so a missing logo is not a broken card.

awards.//: The judged awards, with the definition the GA reads on air while the plate is up. The desk shows title+definition first and reveals the winner on a second press; the winner never enters any feed until that press.
awards.//example: { "id": "directors", "title": "Directors' Award", "description": "For the team that best embodies the spirit of CalGames." }

slides.//: Recognition and info slides: volunteer thank-yous, SystemCore session times, meeting calls, food-truck hours. The side screens rotate the deck on their own; the desk can take any slide to the program. More get typed at the event and persist to data/slides.json.
slides.//kinds: recognition (thank-you card) or info (announcement card). Shout-outs approved from /s/gp join the deck as a third kind.
slides.//example: { "id": "syscore", "kind": "info", "title": "SystemCore session", "lines": ["Saturday 12:30, Room 201", "Limelight walks through the 2027 controller"] }

rundown.//: The day as a list. The desk manager advances it; nothing advances itself, because a rundown that advances on its own will do it during the one delay nobody predicted.
rundown.//matches: A matches block gives a COUNT, not a duration: the length comes from the pace model measuring real cycle time. A printed 7 minutes against a measured 9 is an hour by the end of the day.
rundown.//audience: What the venue screens call the countdown during this segment, e.g. Matches resume.
rundown.//example: { id: quals-am, label: Qualification matches, kind: matches, matches: 24 }

accessibility.//: What the event actually offers, and where. Shown on the venue screens and the phone page, because the person who needs a quiet room is deciding at 11am in a loud building, from a phone. Leave the list empty if the event offers nothing: showing nothing is honest, and inventing a service is worse than silence.
accessibility.//example: { "label": "Quiet room", "detail": "Room 114, past the pits on the left" }
accessibility.//ask: Who to find. A name and a place beats a policy statement.

nexus.//: FRC Nexus: what the QUEUERS are doing. The only source that knows a match is being called before the field does. Read-only over the internet; nothing to do with the field network.
nexus.//apiKey: From frc.nexus/api. Sent as the Nexus-Api-Key header.
nexus.//eventKey: The Nexus event key, usually the same as event.key. Polling starts when both are set.
nexus.//note: Only useful if the event actually runs its queueing on Nexus. For an event that does not, the timings come back looking authoritative and are not.

startgg.//: Side-tournament bracket from start.gg. Metadata only. Round labels and entrants pre-fill the arcade console; the live score stays operator-authoritative because start.gg lags reality by up to a full round (docs/05-arcade.md).
startgg.//token: Personal access token from start.gg -> Developer Settings. Read scope is enough.
startgg.//eventSlug: The EVENT slug, e.g. tournament/calgames-2026-arcade/event/smash-singles. Polling starts when both fields are set.

youtube.//: Google Cloud project -> OAuth 2.0 Client ID (Desktop app), with the YouTube Data API v3 enabled. Scopes needed: https://www.googleapis.com/auth/youtube.upload and https://www.googleapis.com/auth/youtube. The second covers the flip-to-public after TBA linking, and playlists. `npm run auth:youtube` requests both.
youtube.//refreshToken: Obtained once via the OAuth consent flow. Run `npm run auth:youtube` for the walkthrough.
youtube.//before-the-event: Use WRRF's established, verified channel (a new channel's per-day upload cap is low and separate from API quota). Enable live streaming 24h in advance.

tba.//: Request Trusted API access for the event from The Blue Alliance. They issue an auth id and secret per event.
tba.//scope: We publish video and webcasts only. Cheesy Arena owns match data on TBA. We never call matches/update, rankings/update, awards/update, alliance_selections/update, or team_list/update, since those require the FULL dataset and would delete anything not included.
tba.//readKey: Optional. Read APIv3 key for team names and avatars.

stream.//webcastUrl: The public YouTube live URL. Registered on TBA so the event appears on GameDay. TBA does not ingest video. It only embeds this.
